messages:
Carol (CEO): Opening the follow-up thread for pricing & packaging questions from today's all-hands. Drop any clarifications about credits, quotas, rate limits, or plan behavior and we'll respond here.

Sarah (Product): Quick customer question: do Starter promo credits ever roll over month-to-month?

Ashwin (Finance): Not by default. Promo credits expire at month-end unless converted to a short trial or committed credits. We're evaluating a 30-day grace for customers migrating plans.

Mike (Eng): On rate-limits: people asked if throttling is tokens/sec or concurrency-based during deploys. Short answer: both. Edge applies a tokens/sec leaky bucket, plus a per-key concurrency cap to protect streaming sessions.

Sarah (Product): Can we show those defaults in Console (Starter/Pro/Enterprise) so customers can design client-side backoff?

Ashwin (Finance): Yes — we'll publish nominal defaults (e.g., Starter ~100 req/min, 50k tokens/min; Pro ~1k req/min, 500k tokens/min). Enterprise contracts can override and Dedicated installs are configurable.

Carol (CEO): Emphasize these are hosted defaults. Sales/solutions will negotiate caps for Dedicated/private customers.

Mike (Eng): Note: during sustained load adaptive batching may change per-token cost; long sequences batch more efficiently. SRE/SDKs should expose headers to help clients react: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After.

Sarah (Product): We'll draft an FAQ: credits expiry, sample rate-limit table, recommended retry semantics.

Ashwin (Finance): Also piloting a promo->trial conversion program for qualifying accounts; I'll share criteria this week.

OpsBot: docs/console-rate-limits v1.0 deployed to staging at 1793457001 :rocket:

Mike (Eng): I'll add a short eng note and link from the Console FAQ.

Carol (CEO): Sarah/Ashwin sync with Legal on the conversion copy. Thanks everyone.

Sarah (Product): If anyone has customer examples that prompted these questions, DM me and I'll fold them into the FAQ. :thumbsup:
